predecessors.name: Han dynasty
predecessors.text: the whole Han empire as the last Western Han emperors left it (Cliopatria's Han shape of 36 BC to 5 AD, 4.47 M km2, which its first Xin shape repeats within 11 cells)

successors.name: Han dynasty
successors.text: the Xin's last shape, taken by the Gengshi Emperor's restored Han when Chang'an fell on 5 October 23

ledger.x: 9: the Xiongnu stay Wang Mang's tributary.
9: Wang Mang proclaims the Xin at Chang'an.
10: Wang Mang breaks with the Xiongnu.
About 17: the Lülin rebel in Hubei.
About 17: the Chimei rise in southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu.
23: the Xin falls to the rebels.
23: the Xin ends with the Chimei still undefeated in southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu; they go on to take Guanzhong from the Gengshi regime and surrender in 27.
23: Chang'an falls and Wang Mang is killed.
23: the Xin dynasty ends with Wang Mang's death.

wars.name: Wang Mang's war with the Xiongnu
wars.outcome: Wang Mang declared war after the seal dispute and mobilised 300,000 soldiers along the northern border with a plan of twelve armies; no page opened names ground taken or lost.

wars.name: Lülin and Chimei rebellions (fall of the Xin)
wars.outcome: Rebellions from about 17 became a civil war by 19; the Lülin forces, with the Gengshi Emperor proclaimed in early 23, beat the Xin at Kunyang in June-July 23 and took Chang'an on 4-5 October; Wang Mang was killed on 6 October.

certainty.note: The Xin inherited the Han frontiers; the steppe, Tarim and southern frontiers are approximate and the rebel-held lands from 17 have no named boundaries.
